summary: At 3:30 AM on June 5, 1992, the top telepath in the Sol System, S. Dole Melipone, vanishes from the offices of Runciter Associates in New York. The disappearance triggers urgent calls as the Runciter organization realizes it has lost too many PSIs (psychic operatives) in recent months. Glen Runciter learns of the crisis and decides to consult his half-lifer wife, Ella, at the Beloved Brethren Moratorium in Switzerland. Meanwhile, moratorium owner Herbert Schoenheit von Vogelsang oversees the facility where half-lifers are kept in cold-pac suspension, allowing their loved ones brief consultations. Runciter arrives and prepares to speak with Ella about the organization's crisis, establishing the moral and technological framework of the novel's world.

locations.name: Green River, Utah

locations.name: Topeka, Kansas

locations.name: Beloved Brethren Moratorium
locations.context: Swiss facility where half-lifers are preserved in cold-pac; where Ella Runciter is kept

characters.name: Glen Runciter
characters.role_in_chapter: Owner/operator of Runciter Associates; protagonist; aging businessman with artificial organs
characters.key_actions: Takes call about Melipone's disappearance; decides to consult with Ella at the moratorium; exhibits emotional detachment even when alarmed

characters.name: S. Dole Melipone
characters.role_in_chapter: Top telepath who vanishes; generates 68.2 blr units of telepathic aura
characters.key_actions: Disappears without trace; can change physiognomic template frequently

characters.name: Joe Chip
characters.key_actions: Measures the PSI field at the motel and detects Melipone's presence

characters.name: Edie Dorn
characters.role_in_chapter: Inertial (anti-PSI operative) assigned to track Melipone
characters.key_actions: Follows Melipone to Green River, Utah and later to the motel but loses him

characters.name: G. G. Ashwood
characters.role_in_chapter: Telepath and scout for Runciter Associates; enthusiastic, manic energy
characters.key_actions: Reads Melipone at the motel and detects scramble pattern; scouts new talents

characters.name: Ella Runciter
characters.role_in_chapter: Glen's half-lifer wife; 20 years old at death; consulted for organizational advice
characters.key_actions: Awaits consultation at moratorium; Runciter seeks her counsel on crisis management

characters.name: Herbert Schoenheit von Vogelsang
characters.role_in_chapter: Owner/operator of the Beloved Brethren Moratorium
characters.key_actions: Manages daily moratorium operations; takes charge of Ella's case; tends to half-lifers with professional detachment

themes: The nature of PSI abilities and their monopolization
Ambiguity and paranoia in business operations

theological_concepts.context: The existence of half-lifers in cold-pac suspension; temporary reanimation for communication
theological_concepts.theological_frame: Christian resurrection mythology repurposed through technology; echoes of Tibetan Buddhist concepts of bardo (death state)

theological_concepts.context: Half-lifers as intermediaries between living and dead worlds; treated as living information sources
theological_concepts.theological_frame: Shamanic tradition of consulting the dead; spiritualist séance practices

philosophical_concepts.concept: Identity and memory persistence (Melipone's multiple physiognomic templates)
The commodification of consciousness and ability

key_events.significance: Triggers the entire novel's action; represents a pattern of missing PSIs that will drive the plot

key_events.event: Detection of Melipone at the motel via field readings
key_events.significance: Confirms his whereabouts but also demonstrates the technical sophistication of PSI detection
Establishes that half-lifers are valued as advisors despite their limited knowledge; foreshadows Ella's importance to the narrative
